summary.en: Use advanced article patterns for generic meaning, unique references, and common institution phrases.
summary.fa: Use advanced article patterns for generic meaning, unique references, and common institution phrases.

en: Use the with unique items (the sun, the internet).
Use no article for general plural/uncountable nouns (Dogs are friendly, Water is essential).
Use the for specific generic groups when context is shared (the rich, the elderly).
Institutions sometimes drop the article when used for their main purpose (go to school, be in hospital).
fa: Use the with unique items (the sun, the internet).
Use no article for general plural/uncountable nouns (Dogs are friendly, Water is essential).
Use the for specific generic groups when context is shared (the rich, the elderly).
Institutions sometimes drop the article when used for their main purpose (go to school, be in hospital).

en: The moon looks bright tonight. (unique)
Books are useful tools. (generic plural)
She is in hospital after the accident. (institution)
The poor need support. (group reference)
fa: The moon looks bright tonight. (unique)
Books are useful tools. (generic plural)
She is in hospital after the accident. (institution)
The poor need support. (group reference)

summary.en: Use must, might, and can’t to make logical deductions about the present or past based on evidence.
summary.fa: Use must, might, and can’t to make logical deductions about the present or past based on evidence.

en: Present deduction: must/might/can’t + base verb (He must be tired).
Past deduction: must/might/can’t + have + past participle (She might have missed the bus).
Must = strong certainty, might = possibility, can’t = impossible.
Use evidence or clues to support the deduction.
fa: Present deduction: must/might/can’t + base verb (He must be tired).
Past deduction: must/might/can’t + have + past participle (She might have missed the bus).
Must = strong certainty, might = possibility, can’t = impossible.
Use evidence or clues to support the deduction.

en: The lights are off. They must be asleep.
He is not answering. He might be in a meeting.
She can’t be at home; her car is gone.
He must have forgotten the appointment.
fa: The lights are off. They must be asleep.
He is not answering. He might be in a meeting.
She can’t be at home; her car is gone.
He must have forgotten the appointment.
